Table styles

Source: vignettes/articles/table-styles.qmd

A table is drawn in a style named by its role. The report style is the working table of an analysis report. The manuscript style is the table a journal receives, laid out by what the table does: "compare" for groups it compares, "describe" for cohorts or repeated measures it describes side by side.

This page draws one table in each, then prints the matrix of what differs. The matrix is read from hv_table_style() when the page is built, so it is not copied by hand. Some properties are labels the renderers do not read yet; the matrix lists them as the style records them.

One table 

library(hvtiRtables)

The data are gtsummary::trial, a simulated trial that ships with gtsummary. Age is shown as mean±SD and the marker level as a median, so the table also carries the mark the house standard puts on the statistic fewer rows use (¶).

tbl <- hv_tbl_summary(
  gtsummary::trial, by = "trt",
  groups = list(Demography = c("age", "marker"),
                Disease = c("stage", "grade")),
  continuous = c("age", "marker"), categorical = c("stage", "grade"),
  mean_sd = "age", show_variable = FALSE
)
key <- c(SD = "standard deviation")

show_variable = FALSE leaves out the Variable column a report shows on screen. Every saved .docx drops it, and each table here is drawn as it is saved.

The report style 

report <- hv_man_table(tbl)
hv_man_table_save(report, "table-styles-report.docx",
                  abbreviations = key)

What a web page cannot show

The tables above are hv_man_table_display()’s HTML, built from the same code the saver uses for its marks and notes. Fill, grid, spans, weight, alignment, marks and note wording are the saved file’s. Some of the .docx is Word’s alone; open the saved files to see it:

  • The page. Every style saves to US Letter. The report turns landscape when it has three or more statistic columns or is wider than a portrait page; the manuscript turns only on width.
  • The manuscript’s font. The manuscript style sets no font, so in Word the table takes the document’s body font. Here it takes this page’s font.
  • Rows and pages. Row heights in twips, rows kept whole on a page, and the header repeated on a new page are Word’s pagination.
  • Notes and caption. Here the notes are footer lines of the table and the caption a bold line above it. In Word both are paragraphs, the caption above the table and the notes below it, in the same words.
  • The dark theme. The example tables (flextable) are shown on white, as in Word, whatever the site’s theme; the matrix and rules tables below follow the site’s theme. The site’s CSS rule whitens every flextable on the site, the reference examples included.
  • The abbreviation key. In the saved file the key is one paragraph below the notes, in the form Key: A, definition, with each abbreviation in italics (house rule 14). Here it is the same paragraph.

The matrix

The manuscript style takes two columns because its layout is an argument of hv_man_table(), not a property of the style, so one style object serves both tables. A row the same in every style is listed once, after the matrix.

Property report manuscript, compare manuscript, describe
Section row label in the first cell, bold, left; fill on every cell of the row, unmerged spans the full width, bold; filled spans the full width, bold; filled
Borders horizontal rules only full grid: box plus all inner lines, single 0.5 pt full grid: box plus all inner lines, single 0.5 pt
Header one row: a No. column before each group’s <group> N = n; * on the first No., † on each group two rows: Characteristic and n* merged down, the grouping’s name with † spanning its levels; row 2 <level> (N = n) two rows: each group, <level> (N = n), spans its own (n, statistic) pair; row 2 names them, n* and the statistic with †
Non-missing count one column per group one overall n* column one n* column per group, Overall’s included
Note markers the house symbols by meaning, superscript, then a space the house symbols by meaning, at the start of the note, not superscript the house symbols by meaning, at the start of the note, not superscript
Count note Number of non-missing values. Patients with non-missing data. Patients with non-missing data.
Statistic note No. (%) or Median [15th, 85th percentiles]. Values are No. (%) or median [15th, 85th percentiles]. Values are No. (%) or median [15th, 85th percentiles].
Font Times New Roman 12 pt none set: the document’s body font none set: the document’s body font
Caption optional: bold, above the table, when given required: bold, above the table required: bold, above the table
Row height auto at least 300 twips, rows kept on one page at least 300 twips, rows kept on one page
Variable column on screen only; every saved .docx drops it never never
Merged cells none header and section rows header and section rows

What every style shares:

Property Every style
Fill color #CAEDFB; hv_table_style(fill =) sets it
Overall and comparison columns shown when the table carries them
Continuous values 9.9 [8.5, 11], 63±13: the house standard
Categorical values 30 (42): the house standard
Abbreviations Key: A, …; B, …
Alignment and weight header bold; first column left, others centered
Header repeated on a new page yes
Page US Letter, landscape when wide, else portrait

The values are the house standard, which hv_tbl_summary() writes for every style: P values without a leading zero (.013, <.001, >.9), and the statistic fewer rows use marked on its cells, § on a median among means and ¶ on a mean among medians. A journal that prints the submitted table can change the fill: hv_table_style("manuscript", fill = "#A5C9EB").

The house rules

Table Construction for Manuscripts (7/14/2026) was written for tables edited by hand for submission. A generated table is never edited by hand, so a rule that exists to keep a hand-edited table editable became a style property: the report keeps it, and the manuscript keeps it or sets it aside where the submissions did. A content rule says what a reader needs whoever made the table, and binds every style. hv_check_docx() checks the rules marked checked in any saved file; rule 3 is checked as each style keeps it, strictly with style = "report" and allowing header and full-width section merges otherwise.

Rule What it asks Kind report manuscript Checked
2 No blank paragraph where the table is pasted hand edit kept kept
3 No merged cells hand edit kept set aside: merges its header and section rows yes
5 Times New Roman, 12 pt (11 pt for a wide table) hand edit kept set aside: the document’s body font
8 The count note reads “Number of non-missing values.” hand edit kept set aside: “Patients with non-missing data.”
13 Notes below the table, never inside it content kept kept yes
14 One abbreviation key, sorted, below the notes hand edit kept kept
No hidden spacing columns content kept kept yes
No floating layers (text boxes, frames) content kept kept yes
The non-missing count is shown, and its note says what it counts content kept kept
Every statistic is named and every mark explained content kept kept
Every abbreviation in the table is defined content kept kept

Each file saved above passes, checked as the style that wrote it. A count of 0 means the saved file has no findings:

nrow(hv_check_docx("table-styles-report.docx", style = "report"))
#> [1] 0
nrow(hv_check_docx("table-styles-compare.docx", style = "manuscript"))
#> [1] 0
nrow(hv_check_docx("table-styles-describe.docx", style = "manuscript"))
#> [1] 0
